package: @astryxdesign/core

# DropdownMenuGroup

Use DropdownMenuGroup to give related compound-menu rows one visible and programmatic name. Use an untitled group only when a separate name would not help people understand the rows.

Anatomy: Group, Heading (optional), Rows (optional)

## Import

```tsx
import { DropdownMenuGroup } from '@astryxdesign/core/DropdownMenu';
```

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Use short, descriptive title content that explains what the grouped rows have in common.
- **Do:** Keep the title non-interactive so every available action remains in the menu arrow-key order.
- **Don't:** Place buttons, links, fields, or other controls in title. Put them in DropdownMenu header or footer instead.
- **Don't:** Wrap rows that do not form a meaningful set; a group adds structure only when its relationship helps users.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | - | Non-interactive heading content shown above the rows and used as the group's accessible name. Omit for an unnamed group; place controls in DropdownMenu header or footer. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The grouped rows: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, or DropdownMenuSubMenu. |
| `xstyle` | `StyleXStyles` | - | StyleX styles applied to the role="group" wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object. |
| `className` | `string` | - | CSS class name applied to the role="group" wrapper. |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` | - | Inline styles applied to the role="group" wrapper. |
| `ref` | `React.Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | - | Ref forwarded to the role="group" wrapper. |
